gaps.sentence: She was appointed ___ managing director at just thirty-four.
gaps.explanation: After 'appoint/elect/name + unique role' no article is used.

gaps.sentence: She made ___ decision to move to the countryside.
gaps.explanation: 'Make a decision' is the fixed collocation; 'the countryside' is a fixed phrase with 'the'.

gaps.sentence: ___ most people agree that change is needed.
gaps.explanation: 'Most people' in a general sense takes no article.

gaps.sentence: ___ books you left on my desk were really useful.
gaps.explanation: 'The books you left…' — the clause identifies which books.

gaps.sentence: He was elected ___ chairman of the board.
gaps.explanation: No article is used with unique roles after 'elect', 'appoint', 'become'.

gaps.sentence: ___ United Kingdom consists of four countries.
gaps.explanation: 'The United Kingdom', 'the USA', 'the Czech Republic' all take 'the'.

gaps.sentence: He was ___ only person to solve the puzzle.
gaps.explanation: 'The only person' — 'only' makes the noun unique, so 'the'.

gaps.sentence: She works in ___ insurance, not banking.
gaps.explanation: Industry/sector names take no article: in insurance, in banking, in marketing.
